ui_bugs.issue: Red 'Not authenticated' banner shows at top of /wallet for any logged-in user (customer AND owner admin) even though JWT-authorized API calls succeed (deposit/withdraw/list all work). Appears to be a separate (legacy) call inside WalletPage relying on session_token cookie returning 401. Pre-existing, not caused by new funding feature, but it is alarming UX on a money page.

action_items: Investigate the 'Not authenticated' banner on /wallet for logged-in users (looks like a separate /api/wallet/... call expecting session_token cookie returning 401 even though Bearer JWT works for everything else). UX concern on a real-money page.

FundingRequestBody accepts method='card' (FUNDING_METHODS includes 'card') but UI exposes only bank/paypal/wipay; either remove 'card' from backend whitelist or expose it in the UI to keep them aligned.
wallet_payment_methods POST returns the inserted doc with _id intact via doc.pop('_id', None) AFTER returning a reference — verified response is clean (pop runs on doc dict before return; OK).
admin approve endpoint records a txn but does not store reference back to funding_request_id; consider adding for traceability (audit/refunds).

But on UI the over-withdraw toast text was not captured by my selector (sonner) — Sonner uses [data-sonner-toaster]; the actual user-visible toast renders correctly (backend returned 400). No fix required.

rca of the issue: Not applicable - no critical bugs in the new feature. Note on the 'Not authenticated' banner: it likely comes from a /api/wallet/... call inside WalletPage that uses cookie-based credentials (session_token) instead of the Authorization Bearer header used by the new WalletFunding component. The 401s in browser console occur on the wallet page even for the seeded owner admin, confirming it's not a JWT validity issue but an auth-mode mismatch. Mitigation: switch that call to send Authorization: Bearer ${localStorage.token} header consistent with the rest of the app.
